To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) a gene signature associated type 1 cell mediated cytotoxic immunity was associated with increased survival in breast cancer patients and, 2) WISP1 expression was increased in breast cancer and correlated with a gene signature consistent inhibition of IL12.

Wnt-Induced Signaling Protein- 1 (WISP-1) is an oncogenic factor in invasive breast cancer that inhibits type 1 immunity and promotes type 2 immunity, and that type 1 immunity is associated with increased survival in invasive breast cancer patients.
WISP1 expression in invasive breast cancer is associated with reduced overall survival and is associated with reduced type 1 cell mediated cytotoxic immunity.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel approach to identify and validate a gene signature that can be used to predict the outcome of patients with invasive breast cancers.
identifying the molecular basis of immune dysfunction associated with invasive breast cancer.
the molecular mechanisms that regulate innate and adaptive immunity in breast cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gene signature associated with the inhibition of IL12 and type 1 immunity was correlated with WISP1 and that this gene signature was associated with increased mortality in patients with invasive cancer.

the gene expression signature of type 1 immunity was associated with a survival advantage in patients with invasive cancer and that WISP1 was an important paracrine mediator of this gene expression signature.
WISP1 is an important mediator of breast cancer oncogenesis and is a potential therapeutic target.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
WISP1 may be an important paracrine regulator that contributes to breast cancer progression and metastasis by inhibiting type 1 cell- mediated immunity.
WISP1 expression correlates with oncogenic transformation in breast cancer and inhibits type 1 cell mediated cytotoxic immunity through inhibiting the IL12 signaling pathway.
type 1 immunity can be used to stratify patients with invasive breast cancers and that WISP1 is a potential therapeutic target for patients with triple negative breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WISP1-IL12 signaling axis is a promising new target for therapeutic intervention.
the immune signature associated with type-1 cell-mediated immunity is associated with improved survival in invasive breast cancer patients.
